pairs.difference: A: the purple fan is tilted and spread wide across the card, with its fan edge reaching close to the top-right and the handle reaching the left edge, so it reads as one dynamic shape. B: the opera glasses sit almost centered with an even frame of pink diamond background on all sides (margin 0.093). The two barrels face the viewer in a near-frontal, symmetric pose, and the small handle hangs under them. This matches the generated lessons: a complete, centered object with equal breathing room.
pairs.fix: Turn the opera glasses to a strong three-quarter angle and scale them up so the front barrel nearly touches the right edge and the handle reaches toward the bottom-left corner. Let the background show unevenly around them.

pairs.difference: A: the picnic basket sits in a three-quarter view on grass, filling the lower two-thirds, with the handle near the top; it is a typical real framing. B: the boxing gloves are cropped hard at the left and right edges (width 0.951, margin 0.021) and rest on a wooden shelf against blue panels. The tight crop matches real cards like the computer. Neither framing departs from the real set clearly enough to decide.

A: the lace parasol is a self-contained diagonal: the canopy sits in the upper-left and the hooked handle ends at lower-right. The swirl background shows evenly all round (margin 0.102), and the whole object floats with a tidy margin. B: the beach umbrella canopy pushes to the right edge, the pole runs down at a slant, and the canopy is off-balance. That looser, edge-pressing framing is real-like.
pairs.fix: Enlarge the parasol and push the canopy close to the top and right edges, so the curved handle nearly touches the bottom of the card. Avoid even background on every side.

pairs.difference: A: the porch swing canopy runs nearly edge to edge at the top (margin 0.028), a tree trunk is cropped at the right, and the scene fills the card like the real lawn-mower and fan cards. B: the white bench is set in the middle of a gravel path, fully shown with clear space on all sides (margin 0.091, above the real maximum), and the path and bushes fill out the scene around it. This matches the generated lighthouse and computer lessons, which pull back to show the whole object on its setting.
pairs.fix: Move the camera closer to the bench and let its right armrest and back run off the right and top edges. Show less of the gravel path and background trees.

pairs.difference: A: the roller coaster cars and loop track are cropped by the left, right and bottom edges, with a strong curve leading in from the top-left; this is real-style cropping. B: the keyboard on its X-stand is in a diagonal three-quarter view, fills the card well, and the music-note background is quiet. Both framings sit inside the real range, and neither shows the generated habit of a centered, frontal, padded object.

A: the scout jacket is turned three-quarters, with sleeves reaching both sides, and the sash and badges make a clear diagonal. B: the top hat floats dead-center in a rays background, upright and nearly symmetric, with even yellow margins all round (0.098, near the real top). It is the composed, padded, centered look of the generated lessons.
pairs.fix: Tilt the top hat on a steeper angle and make it bigger, so the brim nearly touches the left and right edges. Shift the crown toward the top-right so the spacing is uneven.

pairs.difference: A: the teacup and saucer sit low and centered on a wide tablecloth. The box is short and wide (height 0.55, near the real minimum), and a large band of tablecloth fills the lower third with no subject in it. B: the fountain fills the card in height (0.769) and its basin is cropped by the sides and bottom, which is real-like. A's flat side-on view with a big empty foreground matches the generated computer lesson, which shows the setting under the object.
pairs.fix: Bring the camera closer and look down at the teacup a little more, so the saucer fills the bottom half and the rim nearly reaches the left and right edges. Cut down the visible tablecloth.

pairs.difference: A: the red Georgian door is small, narrow (width 0.428, below the real range) and centered on a large stone wall, with steps, pavement, bushes and ivy in all four corners. The door is not the first read; the wall is. B: the blue door is cropped by all edges, and the wreath fills the center as a clear focal point, like the real lighthouse crop. A matches the generated lessons, which pull back to show the full object in a scene.
pairs.fix: Fill the card with the red door: crop the arch at the top and the step at the bottom, show only a thin strip of stone wall at each side, and drop the corner bushes.

pairs.difference: A: the golf club runs off the top-right edge and the head and ball fill the lower-left, which is a bold real-style crop on grass. B: the brass spyglass floats small in the middle of the striped cyan background. It occupies 0.168 area with height 0.452, both below the real range, and leaves wide empty margins (0.116). At thumbnail size it reads as a small stick in a big empty field.
pairs.fix: Draw the spyglass much larger, running corner to corner from the bottom-right to the top-left, with the big lens end nearly touching the top-left edge and the eyepiece near the bottom-right.

pairs.difference: A: the vending machine stands in a three-quarter view, tall in the frame (height 0.79), with its front angled toward the viewer. B: the floral teapot is placed side-on and centered, with the lid knob and spout symmetric, and empty purple space above and below (height 0.625). It shows the generated habit of a frontal, centered, evenly padded object.
pairs.fix: Turn the teapot to a three-quarter view, seen slightly from above, and make it bigger, so the spout nearly reaches the right edge and the lid knob sits near the top.

pairs.difference: A: the red neckerchief fills the card top to bottom (height 0.833) and the badge sits at the center as a clear focal point. B: the straw bonnet is a flat, wide ellipse stretched edge to edge (width 0.942, height 0.492, below the real range), with a band of empty green above and below. The bow pulls focus to the right side.
pairs.fix: Tip the bonnet toward the viewer so the crown and brim fill more of the height. Keep the brim inside the left and right edges, and leave less empty green above and below.

pairs.difference: A: the taxi is in a bold three-quarter view, large, with its nose near the left edge and road stripes leading the eye in. B: the pram sits in the middle of a big cobblestone floor, which fills the lower half. The thin handle and spoked wheels give it little visual weight (area 0.244), so the cobbles compete with it at thumbnail size. That matches the generated lessons, which show the object on a full setting.
pairs.fix: Move the camera closer so the pram fills most of the card, with its hood and basket in the upper middle and the wheels near the bottom edge. Show only a little ground under it, and use a plain rays background.

pattern: Generated cards pull back and show the whole object, complete and centered. They sit it in an even frame of background, or put it in a full little scene with ground, setting and props, and use a more frontal, symmetric pose. Real cards crop harder, tilt the object, let it press on one or two edges, and make the hero the first read with little scene around it. Thin or flat generated objects (spyglass, bonnet, pram, door) also fall below the real occupancy and height range.
